subject: Re: Private/VPC Pricing - follow up and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Private/VPC Pricing - follow up and next steps

Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion and appreciate the openness on volume and procurement timing. Short recap and a few asks so we can put a tight proposal together for Private (VPC) deployment: 

Recap from our call
- Goal: host customer-facing recommendation/UIs on FinTechCo infra in a VPC with audit logging and KMS integration.
- Target go-live: pilot in Q3 with production rollout in Q4.
- Primary model workloads: chat + high-throughput embeddings for search/ranking.

Asks / data points to finalize pricing: 
1) Expected token volumes: best guess for month 1, month 3, and steady-state (tokens/month). If you have ranges that’s fine (e.g., 100M–300M/month).
2) Budget envelope: is there an internal target (monthly or annual) we should aim to stay within?
3) Unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens the finance team wants to see?
4) Environments: how many separate deployments do you want (prod / staging / dev / regional instances)?
5) Licensing model preference: term license (annual platform fee + usage), or prefer a pure committed usage discount structure?
6) Support tier needed: Standard, Premium (faster SLAs), or Enterprise (named support + quarterly reviews)?

I’ve attached a short pricing summary that outlines typical Private licensing options and support tiers — it includes sample unit costs at different commit levels so you can see order-of-magnitude numbers.

If you can reply with the items above, I’ll circulate a tailored commercial (license + example unit cost at your volumes) and a draft SOW for procurement. If easier, we can run a quick 30-min pricing review this week — Marissa (cc’d) can join to map the deployment topology.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Ben —

Thanks for the summary — great to have this in writing. Below are the numbers we discussed (high-level):

1) Volumes (estimates)
- Month 1 (pilot): ~50M tokens/month
- Month 3: ~150M tokens/month
- Steady-state (end of year): 200M–250M tokens/month (conservative)

2) Budget envelope
- For platform + infra we’re scoped at roughly $150k–$300k ARR for the first year (flexible depending on pricing shape).

3) Unit economics target
- Finance would prefer to see ~$600–800 per 1M tokens for hosted/private unit costs (we know this varies by commit/support).

4) Environments
- 1 Prod (multi-AZ in our VPC)
- 1 Staging
- 2 Dev sandboxes (shared)

5) Licensing model
- Prefer a term license with an annual platform fee + discounted committed usage. Procurement likes predictable fixed fees for vendor relationships.

6) Support
- Ideally Premium (faster SLAs) but open to Enterprise if the price delta isn’t material.

Procurement timeline
- We’d like commercial terms by mid-August to align approvals and budget cycles — aiming to sign in Q3.

Let me know if you need a more granular month-by-month token projection — we can share our internal forecast if helpful.

Regards,
Alex Reyes
Head of Data Products | FinTechCo
alex@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reyes <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private/VPC Pricing - follow up and next steps

Alex —

Appreciate the details — that’s exactly what we need to build a commercial that maps to your procurement preferences. High-level guidance on how Redwood typically structures Private/VPC deals, and what that will look like at the volumes you quoted: 

Commercial components (summary)
- Annual Platform License (fixed): covers control plane, console, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, feature flagging for rollouts. Typical range: $50k – $150k/year depending on support tier and number of environments/regions.
- Committed Usage Pricing (buckets): committed token tiers reduce unit cost significantly. Typical unit-cost bands (examples):
  - Pay-as-you-go / Minimal commit: ~$900 / 1M tokens
  - 12-mo moderate commit: ~$600 / 1M tokens
  - Enterprise multi-year commit: ~$400–$500 / 1M tokens
- Minimum throughput/reserved capacity surcharge: for guaranteed low-latency production we size reserved GPU capacity; surcharge depends on qps/seq-length profile.
- Support add-on: Premium (faster SLAs) adds ~10–20% to license fee; Enterprise support includes named CSM/AM and quarterly QBRs.

Rough example (using your steady-state 200M tokens/month = 2.4B tokens/year)
- If you take a 12-mo commit at $600 / 1M: usage cost ≈ $1,440,000/year (2,400 * $600) — note this is illustrative; Private deals typically combine a platform license + committed unit cost discounts and sometimes a blended cap.
- For Private, customer often chooses a larger platform license and multi-year commit to bring unit cost down (example: $100k license + $400 / 1M committed pricing → ~ $960k/year usage + license).

Based on your target $600–$800/1M and the budget envelope you mentioned ($150k–$300k ARR), the most likely commercial shape we should explore is:
- A mid-size platform license (~$75k–$125k/year) + a committed usage tier at ~$600 / 1M with an initial 12-mo commit.
- For materially lower unit cost (~$400 / 1M) we’d expect a larger multi-year commit and/or a higher license fee.

Action items / next steps
1) Can you confirm the steady-state monthly token target we should model (200M vs 250M)?
2) Confirm desired support tier (Standard / Premium / Enterprise).
3) Confirm number of distinct deployments (we’ll price per-environment if you want isolated VPCs per region/customer).
4) I’ll share a tailored commercial and a draft SOW (attached) — Marissa will join the next call to walk the topology and sizing.

I attached the short pricing summary PDF with the ranges above and a sample SOW template. If it’s helpful, we can run a 30-min pricing workshop this week to align on commit level vs license sizing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Summary.pdf, SOW_template.docx
